lyrics:
[Intro: piano and soft steel guitar]

[Verse 1: plain male baritone, storytelling]
My neighbor got the phone call on a Wednesday, half past ten
The kind you wait two weeks for, where they say it's clear, or when
All clear. I asked him at the fence what he did with news like that
He set his coffee on the post and tipped back his hat

[Chorus: full band rises, strings]
He said, "I went home for lunch
I sat down while it was hot
I asked my wife about her morning
And I listened, like it or not
I didn't climb a mountain, didn't jump out of a plane
I went home for lunch
And I've done it every day"

[Verse 2: baritone, band soft]
He said, "I always thought I'd travel, thought I'd buy that boat
Thought the big stuff was the stuff a man would want to hold
Then I'm sitting in that paper gown and all that I could see
Was a Tuesday grilled cheese sandwich and her sitting across from me"

[Chorus: full band rises, strings]
He said, "I went home for lunch
I sat down while it was hot
I asked my wife about her morning
And I listened, like it or not
I didn't climb a mountain, didn't jump out of a plane
I went home for lunch
And I've done it every day"

[Bridge: building toward the key lift]
"I coach the little league now, and I'm terrible at that
I call my brother Sundays and we don't talk about the past
I'm not doing more," he said. "I'm doing it awake."
Then his wife called from the kitchen, and he said, "That's my break."

[Final Chorus: key change up, in the singer's own voice]
So I went home for lunch
I sat down while it was hot
I asked my wife about her morning
And I listened, and I learned a lot
I'm not waiting on a phone call to tell me what to do
I went home for lunch
You should, too

[Outro: steel guitar, a kitchen chair pulled out]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 76 BPM, 4/4, G major, lifting to A major for the last chorus. A slow story ballad that grows.

VOICE: Male baritone, plain, warm and conversational, quoting his neighbour in a slightly lower, drier tone. He opens up to full voice in the choruses and holds the last note of the final one.

INSTRUMENTS: Piano, pedal steel guitar, acoustic guitar, bass, soft drums building through the song, a full string section from the second chorus, a fiddle doubling the melody at the end.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano and steel. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:48 Chorus 1. 1:20 Verse 2. 1:54 Chorus 2. 2:26 Bridge, building. 2:54 Final chorus, key up. 3:28 Outro, steel guitar and a chair at 3:40.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2000s country ballad: warm, full and cinematic, strings wide, voice central and honest.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The key change at 2:54, when 'he said' becomes 'so I'.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original answers death with a list of adventures. This one answers good news with attention: the same life, lived awake. It is a correction that only someone older would make.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Curious, surprised, convinced, changed.
